lead.tldr: CoreWeave's $6B Jane Street contract signals rising demand for GPU cloud in crypto trading and AI workloads • Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI could automate zero‑day discovery, prompting exchanges to secure AI‑defence capabilities now • Apple’s removal of fake Ledger app highlights ongoing App Store vetting gaps, custodial wallet providers must strengthen brand verification • Bitwise’s Avalanche ETF with 70% staking introduces yield‑focused crypto products, raising regulatory scrutiny on on‑chain income reporting • Rakuten’s integration of XRP into loyalty‑point exchanges signals Japanese conglomerates’ push for crypto mainstream adoption, may boost XRP demand • Bitcoin’s price hovering near $76k with profit‑taking on 63k BTC suggests short‑term consolidation, limiting upside for next week

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today we see massive infrastructure bets from CoreWeave and eToro, escalating AI‑driven security concerns on exchanges. And heightened regulatory focus from Warren’s Musk warning, plus Bitnomial’s US‑compliant futures and Rakuten’s XRP rollout.

top_signals.title: CoreWeave Announces $6B Deal With Trading Firm Jane Street
top_signals.summary: CoreWeave announced a $6 billion contract with the trading firm Jane Street. Under the agreement CoreWeave will supply GPU-accelerated cloud compute services to support Jane Street’s trading operations. The partnership underscores the growing demand among institutional traders for high‑performance infrastructure to handle crypto‑related trading and AI workloads.

top_signals.title: ‘AI-based super attacker’ threat looms as top crypto exchanges scramble for access to powerful Claude model
top_signals.summary: Anthropic’s new AI model Claude Mythos can autonomously discover zero‑day vulnerabilities. The capability has prompted leading crypto exchanges such as Coinbase and Binance to race for access as a defensive measure. Security experts warn the model could expose the crypto stack to losses ranging from hundreds of millions to billions of dollars.

top_signals.title: Apple defends App Store record after fake Ledger app drains $10m in Bitcoin and Solana
top_signals.summary: A malicious fake Ledger wallet app listed on the Apple App Store stole nearly $10 million in Bitcoin and Solana from more than 50 victims. Apple responded by removing the app and suspending the developer’s account. Investigators traced the illicit proceeds through the KuCoin exchange and a centralized mixing service. The incident highlights the need for heightened vetting of mobile wallet applications and reinforces the importance of robust custody controls for institutional crypto exposure.

top_signals.title: Elizabeth Warren slams Elon Musk over X Money’s rumored crypto feature
top_signals.summary: U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren has written to Elon Musk to express concerns about X’s planned payments service, X Money. She warns that the feature could create consumer protection, national security, and financial stability risks, particularly if it includes stablecoins. The letter underscores growing regulatory attention to the platform as it expands beyond social media into financial services. Institutional investors should monitor the potential for heightened oversight that could affect X’s ability to operate as a de facto financial institution.

top_signals.title: Bitwise Launchdx Avalanche ETF with Staking Exposure
top_signals.summary: Bitwise Asset Management has introduced a new exchange‑traded fund that provides direct exposure to the Avalanche blockchain. The BAVA spot Avalanche ETF is listed on the NYSE and stakes roughly 70 percent of its AVAX holdings to earn yield for investors. Shares trade at $25.50 and the fund charges a 0.34 percent sponsor fee, which is waived for the first month on the initial $500 million of assets. The product expands the range of crypto‑focused ETFs available to institutional investors seeking diversified digital‑asset exposure.

top_signals.title: Bitnomial Launches US-Regulated Injective Futures with ETF Implications
top_signals.summary: Bitnomial has introduced a US‑regulated futures product on the Injective layer‑2 exchange, marking the first such offering that meets U.S. securities rules. The product provides institutional investors with a compliant way to gain exposure to crypto assets through futures contracts on a regulated platform. Bitnomial says the launch is intended to serve as a stepping stone toward broader crypto‑ETF adoption and expands the range of regulated derivatives available on the platform.

top_signals.title: Rakuten makes XRP move as Japanese conglomerates target crypto markets
top_signals.summary: Rakuten will allow its e‑pay users to convert loyalty points into XRP and other digital assets and to pay with XRP at participating retailers. This capability integrates a major cryptocurrency into a widely used Japanese payment ecosystem, expanding retail exposure to crypto. The initiative reflects a wider trend among Japanese conglomerates such as Mercari and Mitsubishi to embed crypto services in consumer products, indicating growing institutional interest in mainstream adoption.

top_signals.title: eToro shares jump on news of Zengo acquisition in crypto and prediction market move
top_signals.summary: eToro disclosed that it will acquire self‑custody crypto wallet Zengo for a reported $70 million to broaden its tokenisation and prediction‑market capabilities. The announcement lifted eToro’s share price by roughly 5 percent, taking the company’s market valuation to about $3 billion. The deal signals eToro’s strategic push to integrate custodial solutions and expand its product suite for institutional and retail investors in the rapidly growing crypto and prediction‑market sectors.

top_signals.title: Iran's Bitcoin toll 'virtually impossible' to collect, says policy institute
top_signals.summary: Iran has announced plans to accept Bitcoin for toll payments through the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts say the current Bitcoin network and its Lightning layer lack the speed, cost efficiency, and liquidity needed for large‑scale toll settlements. The policy reflects Tehran’s broader strategy to adopt censorship‑resistant financial rails. However, stablecoins remain vulnerable to freezes by issuers such as Tether, highlighting ongoing regulatory and operational risks.

top_signals.title: Crypto PAC Fellowship Discloses $11M from Cantor Fitzgerald and Anchorage
top_signals.summary: The Crypto PAC Fellowship, a political action committee that promotes crypto‑industry interests, has disclosed a new funding round. It received $11 million from Cantor Fitzgerald, a financial services firm, and Anchorage, a provider of crypto‑custody solutions. The capital will be used to finance the fellowship’s advocacy work and development projects aimed at shaping regulatory policy. Institutional investors are watching the partnership because coordinated lobbying can affect the regulatory environment and market dynamics for digital assets.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Stalls at $76K As Profit-Taking Hit 63K BTC
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin is holding near $76,000 after its latest rally. Traders have realized profits on roughly 63,000 BTC, which contributed to the price stalling. The near‑1% daily gain and resulting price stability suggest a short‑term consolidation phase rather than a decisive directional shift, a pattern that institutional investors monitor for entry timing and risk management.

top_signals.title: BTC price pulls back as $75,000 remains 'both the milestone and the ceiling:' Crypto Markets Today
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin is trading below the $75,000 resistance level, a price point described as both a milestone and a ceiling for market participants. The pullback in Bitcoin has dragged leading altcoins such as Ethereum, XRP and Solana lower, underscoring the inter‑asset correlation that can affect portfolio exposure. Futures markets have recorded $424 million in liquidations, split evenly between longs and shorts, signaling heightened uncertainty that may influence risk‑adjusted allocation decisions for institutional investors.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past month has reminded us how quickly the crypto landscape can shift from opportunity to urgency. CoreWeave just announced a six‑billion dollar contract with the trading firm Jane Street. By providing GPU‑accelerated cloud compute, CoreWeave is giving institutional traders the horsepower they need for both high‑frequency crypto trading and AI‑driven strategies. This partnership is a clear signal that the demand for specialized infrastructure is moving beyond niche labs into mainstream finance. At the same time, the emergence of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos has sparked a new kind of race. The model can autonomously discover zero‑day vulnerabilities and exchanges such as Coinbase and Binance are scrambling to secure access as a defensive shield. Security experts warn that without proper safeguards the crypto stack could face losses measured in billions. Finally, the recent fake Ledger wallet app that stole nearly ten million dollars in Bitcoin and Solana from more than fifty users underscores the importance of rigorous vetting. Apple’s swift removal of the app and suspension of the developer’s account show that platform operators can act quickly, yet the incident also highlights the need for stronger custody controls for institutional exposure. As investors and builders, how do we balance the push for cutting‑edge compute and AI with the imperative to protect users and assets? #Web3 #Crypto #Blockchain #CryptoVC
